mcqs.q: In this male-only Australian sample, which group demonstrated the highest animal empathy?
mcqs.e: Pet-ownership-experience men scored significantly higher in animal empathy than farmers or low-experience men.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude was most influential in developing animal empathy?
o: The responsibility and sacrifice involved in pet caring
mcqs.e: Not all experiences were equal—the responsibility and sacrifice of pet caring appeared most influential.

mcqs.q: What did all three groups most strongly endorse as shaping their beliefs about how animals think and feel?
o: Direct interactions with animals in adulthood
mcqs.e: All groups highly endorsed direct adult interactions with animals as most influential to their beliefs.

mcqs.q: The highest-priority canine welfare research issues identified most often concerned:
mcqs.e: Most top-priority issues related to the human-canine relationship, such as ownership and behavioral problems.

mcqs.q: Which topic area was identified as previously 'most underfunded'?
o: Real-world welfare issues, especially dog breeding and supply
mcqs.e: The most underfunded priorities were real-world welfare issues, particularly breeding and supply of dogs.

mcqs.q: Among common chronic primary-care disorders, which were flagged as most underfunded (2012–2022)?
o: Periodontal disease, anal sac disorders, overgrown nails, and patellar luxation
mcqs.e: Historical funding analysis flagged periodontal disease, anal sac disorders, overgrown nails, and patellar luxation as most underfunded.

mcqs.q: Compared with current and non-shelter vets, previous shelter veterinarians reported lower rankings for:
o: Interactions with admin staff, multi-vet teams, and mentorship
mcqs.e: Previous shelter vets ranked lower on admin-staff interactions, being part of a multi-vet team, and mentorship availability.

mcqs.q: Which factor did the authors suggest may increase willingness to stay in shelter medicine?
o: Participation in patient decision-making and shelter management procedures
mcqs.e: Vets involved in patient decision-making and shelter management procedures appeared more willing to continue in the field.

mcqs.q: Previous shelter veterinarians were significantly more likely than others to report feeling:
o: Unhappy and left out at work
mcqs.e: Previous shelter vets more often reported feeling unhappy and left out at work.

mcqs.q: Personal and organizational factors explained the greatest variance in which ProQOL component?
mcqs.e: Both factor sets explained the most variance in burnout (~45–48%).

mcqs.q: ProQOL accounted for more variance in intentions to:
mcqs.e: ProQOL explained 28.9% of variance in leaving one's current role versus only 16.0% for leaving the profession.

mcqs.q: The authors concluded that fostering wellbeing and retention requires attention to:
mcqs.e: Both personal and organizational factors significantly predicted ProQOL outcomes.

mcqs.q: How did veterinary support staff compare with veterinarians on wellbeing measures?
o: Lower wellbeing/mental health and higher burnout
mcqs.e: Support staff scored lower in wellbeing and mental health and higher in burnout than veterinarians.

mcqs.q: Regarding suicide ideation over the study period, the study found:
mcqs.e: Burnout stayed high, but there was no increase in suicide ideation.

mcqs.q: Which employer strategy did the authors recommend?
o: Creating safe environments and reducing mental-health stigma
mcqs.e: Employers should build safe environments where staff feel comfortable seeking help and reduce stigma.

mcqs.q: In which country did veterinarians perform the most euthanasia per month?
mcqs.e: Monthly euthanasia counts were significantly highest in Sweden.

mcqs.q: The reported mental burden of euthanasia was highest in which group?
mcqs.e: Mental burden was lowest in Sweden and highest in Jordan; males reported lower burden than females.

mcqs.q: Veterinarians who performed more euthanasia per month reported:
mcqs.e: Higher euthanasia frequency was associated with a lower reported ethical burden.

mcqs.q: Counterintuitively, witnesses comforted by a black facility dog were perceived as:
o: Less sad, less emotional, and happier than with a white dog
mcqs.e: Participants rated witnesses as less sad, less emotional, and happier when comforted by a black dog.

mcqs.q: In adoption centers, Black Dog Bias is reported to be associated with:
o: Higher euthanasia rates for black dogs
mcqs.e: Black dogs are reportedly discriminated against in adoption, resulting in higher euthanasia rates.

mcqs.q: The authors' overall conclusion about facility dogs in courtrooms was that they:
o: Are more beneficial than harmful and do not unfairly sway juries
mcqs.e: Findings supported facility dogs as more beneficial than harmful, without unfairly swaying juries.

mcqs.q: Which theoretical framework guided this study of shelter-worker wellbeing?
mcqs.e: The study applied the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model.

mcqs.q: Job crafting predicted shelter-worker wellbeing:
o: Only before controlling for demands and resources
Even after controlling for job demands and resources
mcqs.e: Job crafting added unique predictive variance for engagement and exhaustion after controlling for demands/resources.

mcqs.q: Which outcome was related to worker performance?
mcqs.e: Work engagement (not exhaustion) was related to performance; both related to intentions to leave.

mcqs.q: How many of the reviewed instruments specifically targeted animal health care professionals?
mcqs.e: Only the ProQOL-5 Veterinary Medicine Version specifically targeted animal health care professionals.

mcqs.q: The content validity of the reviewed compassion-fatigue PROMs was rated as:
o: Insufficient, with low overall evidence quality
mcqs.e: All reviewed PROMs had insufficient content validity and low overall evidence quality.

mcqs.q: The review's main conclusion was that:
o: Existing CF instruments are well validated
Further robust research on CF measurement is needed
mcqs.e: The authors called for further robust methodology to address the identified measurement flaws.

mcqs.q: After ground transport, 8-week-old puppies showed which change during isolation testing?
o: Decreased exploration with increased locomotion and escape attempts
mcqs.e: Post-transport puppies explored less and showed more locomotion and escape attempts.

mcqs.q: Physiological markers (fecal glucocorticoid metabolites and sIgA) after transport:
mcqs.e: Both FGM and fecal sIgA increased post-transport, indicating distress.

mcqs.q: The authors interpreted increased post-transport affiliative behavior as:
o: Puppies seeking social support as a coping strategy
mcqs.e: Higher affiliative behavior likely reflected puppies seeking social support to cope with transport distress.

mcqs.q: The most common reason the CDC denied dogs entry in 2020 was:
mcqs.e: Falsified rabies vaccination certificates accounted for 56% of denials.

mcqs.q: Compared with the 2018–2019 averages, dogs denied entry in 2020:
mcqs.e: The 458 dogs denied entry in 2020 represented a 52% increase over prior-year averages.

mcqs.q: The increased import attempts of inadequately vaccinated dogs were attributed mainly to:
mcqs.e: The rise was linked to increased demand for domestic pets during the COVID-19 pandemic.

mcqs.q: Both studies found that owner-dog relationships for imported (non-Canadian-sourced) dogs were:
o: Significantly poorer than for Canadian-born dogs
Not poorer than for Canadian-born dogs
mcqs.e: Neither study found evidence of a poorer owner-dog relationship for imported dogs.

mcqs.q: Owners of Canadian-sourced dogs were more likely to:
o: Use harsh training methods and hold higher expectations for their dog
mcqs.e: Owners of Canadian-sourced dogs used harsh training methods more often and had higher expectations.

mcqs.q: These two surveys were conducted among dog owners in:
mcqs.e: Both online surveys sampled dog owners in British Columbia, Canada.
